title: Jianghu: Wuxia and Xianxia Sound Effects
shortText: 133 wuxia and xianxia sound effects: jade, iron, silk and qi. Five Phases, cultivation, flying sword. WAV + OGG.
html:
A complete sound suite for a wuxia or xianxia RPG

133 sounds built from one palette of jade, porcelain, lacquered wood, iron, silk and paper: menus, dialogue, the jian and the dao, martial arts, the Five Phases, cultivation, the flying sword, formations and talismans, rewards, encounters, stingers and 5 seamless ambiences.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 29 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files, at least one from every slot. The five Five Phases strikes, all three qi tiers so you can stack them yourself, a breakthrough, the flying sword's whole lifecycle, and a 24 second mountain peak ambience.

What is in it

  • Menu and UI (16)
  • Dialogue (6)
  • Blades (14)
  • Martial arts (12)
  • Five Phases (15)
  • Cultivation (13)
  • Flying sword (6)
  • Formations and talismans (8)
  • Jade and porcelain (8)
  • Paper and silk (10)
  • Rewards (8)
  • Encounter and turn (7)
  • Stingers (5)
  • Ambience (5)

The Five Phases

Metal, wood, water, fire and earth each ship a cast, a strike and a ward, named phase_form so a spell system indexes the pair. Measured on the shipped files: in every phase the three forms differ, and in every form the five phases differ (15 form pairs and 30 phase pairs, 0 too close).

Cultivation

Qi gathering is three loops of the same length. Start tier 1 as the player begins to gather, fade in tier 2 and then tier 3 as the charge builds, and hold for as long as the button is held: the 3 stacks are re-summed from the shipped files and every one wraps cleanly. Then the release: a minor breakthrough, a major one and a new realm, each longer than the last, a meridian opening, heavenly tribulation strikes over a seamless storm, stabilising, and a qi deviation for when it goes wrong.

Three lifecycles

Flying sword, Formation array, Talisman: each ships its start, a seamless loop while it runs, its stop and the way it fails (the sword shatters, the array breaks, the talisman fizzles out). 12 states, every loop flag read out of the file.

Takes that actually vary

18 variation sets for the sounds a game repeats (cursors, blips, slashes, palm strikes, blocks, dodges, sword strikes, sleeves, brush strokes, spirit stones and more). Every set's takes differ in both length and brightness, measured on the shipped files, so a random pick never machine guns.

Already own Akatsuki?

Jianghu is the Chinese setting sibling of Akatsuki: Anime / JRPG Sound Suite. They share a grammar, not sounds: all 48 roles the two packs have in common were measured against each other from both packs' files and every one is a different sound. No bells, gongs, bamboo or katana here; those are Akatsuki's.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 13 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG: five ambiences, the three qi tiers, the

gathering storm, the sword in flight, the formation's hum, a burning talisman and a robe in the wind. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 2.61 dB.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1222 checks, 0 failed. 4 ladder steps, all climbing.
  • Nothing in it is music: every pitched sound is one struck object, never a phrase, so it sits under any soundtrack.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings of real jade, porcelain or swords. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Akatsuki: Anime / JRPG Sound Suite, the same grammar for a Japanese setting.
  • Sixfold: Elemental Casting Chains, spells as whole cast, travel and impact chains.
  • Steel and Bone: Medieval Combat Impacts, what hits what, as a grid.
